title: Equivariant and Invariant Message Passing for Global Subseasonal-to-seasonal Forecasting

problem.claim: Accurate forecasting on the subseasonal-to-seasonal timescale is important for agricultural planning and extreme weather preparation.

gap.claim: Existing Transformer-based approaches suffer from biases caused by planar projections of spherical geometry and inadequate handling of vector-scalar variable interactions.

contributions.claim: A graph-based Equivariant and Invariant Message Passing framework is proposed to process spherical grid data directly.
The framework uses SO(3)-equivariant embeddings for vector data, SO(3)-invariant embeddings for scalar data, and a shared invariant message embedding for their interaction.
It proposes message-aggregation functions that update embeddings while enforcing strict equivariant and invariant symmetry constraints.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 41 years of ERA5 reanalysis data reportedly show significant improvement over advanced data-driven models and ECMWF numerical systems.
The authors report empirically superior geometric predictions and ablation studies supporting the efficacy of the design.

narrative_sequence.summary: S2S forecasting is presented as important for societal planning and extreme weather preparation.
Existing data-driven Transformer approaches are described as limited by projection-induced geometric bias and weak vector-scalar interaction handling.
The paper introduces a graph-based framework that directly processes spherical grid data using equivariant and invariant representations.
The authors report improvements over advanced data-driven and ECMWF numerical systems, along with geometric-prediction and ablation results.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework separates symmetry behavior for vector and scalar variables and connects them through invariant messages.

interpretation.claim: Representing variables according to their transformation properties may help preserve geometric structure in spherical forecasting tasks.

application.claim: For other spatial prediction problems with mixed vector and scalar fields, consider symmetry-aware representations and aggregation functions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers beyond the reported forecasting setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify forecast horizons, evaluation metrics, baseline configurations, or numerical improvement magnitudes.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or reproducibility information.
The abstract does not establish performance across datasets or conditions beyond the reported ERA5 experiments.
